description: Oryza sativa: a tillering grass grown in flooded fields.

diseases.name: Rice Blast
diseases.description: The most damaging disease of rice: diamond-shaped leaf lesions and broken necks of the panicle.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by wind; long dew, cool nights and high nitrogen favour it.
symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown borders
Neck rot: the panicle base turns black and breaks
diseases.effect: Leaf blast kills seedlings; neck blast empties the panicles.
diseases.untreated: Can destroy most of a crop.

steps.title: Scout leaves and necks
steps.instruction: Check for diamond lesions and blackened necks.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide at the advised growth stages on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

steps.title: Cut back nitrogen
steps.instruction: Split the nitrogen and avoid heavy doses.

lifecycle: Spores blow from infected rice.
Long dew lets them infect.
Diamond-shaped lesions form on the leaves.
Spores spread to the panicle necks.

diseases.name: Sheath Blight
diseases.description: A soil-borne fungal disease of rice leaf sheaths, worst in dense, heavily fertilised crops.
diseases.causes: Fungal resting bodies float on the flood water and infect the sheaths at the water line; it climbs in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Oval, grey-green, water-soaked lesions on the sheaths near the water
Lesions bleach with brown borders, like snakeskin
Spreads up the plant; leaves die
diseases.untreated: Yield losses in dense, high-nitrogen crops.

steps.title: Scout the water line
steps.instruction: Check the lower sheaths in dense patches.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide if it climbs on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Resting bodies float on the flood water.
They infect the sheaths at the water line.
Snakeskin lesions climb the plant.
New resting bodies drop into the field.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: rice sheath blight

diseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
diseases.description: One of the most serious rice diseases: leaves yellow and dry from the tips and edges.
diseases.causes: Bacteria enter through leaf pores and wounds and spread in irrigation water, rain and wind; storms and heavy nitrogen favour it.
symptoms: Water-soaked to yellow stripes along the leaf edges, starting at the tip
Stripes turn straw-white with a wavy edge
Milky drops of bacterial ooze on young lesions in the morning
diseases.effect: Dried leaves cut grain fill; seedlings can wilt (kresek).
diseases.untreated: Epidemics after storms can halve yields.

steps.title: Drain the field briefly
steps.instruction: Drain and let the field dry for a few days if advised.

steps.title: Hold back nitrogen
steps.instruction: Skip or split the next nitrogen dose.

steps.title: Clean up stubble and weeds
steps.instruction: Remove infected stubble, straw and grass weeds after harvest.
steps.rationale: They carry the bacteria to the next crop.

prevention.title: Avoid flowing water from infected fields
prevention.detail: Water carries it field to field.

lifecycle: Bacteria survive in stubble, straw and weeds.
Water and wind carry them to leaves.
They enter through pores and wounds at the leaf edge.
Stripes spread down from the tip and ooze spreads it.

diseases.name: Brown Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of rice that is worst in poor, nutrient-short soils; it caused the 1943 Bengal famine.
diseases.causes: The fungus comes in on seed and debris; spores spread by wind in warm, humid weather, mostly on stressed, poorly fed rice.
symptoms: Oval, brown spots the size of a sesame seed, with grey centres
A yellow halo round older spots
Spots on the grain husks; discoloured, light grain
diseases.effect: Spotted leaves and grain cut yield and quality.
diseases.untreated: Severe on poor soils, where it can destroy much of the crop.

steps.title: Feed the soil
steps.instruction: Correct potassium, silicon and nitrogen shortages as advised.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide where advised on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Balanced fertiliser
prevention.detail: Nutrient-starved rice is the most susceptible.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on seed and debris.
Wind carries spores to the leaves.
Oval brown spots form, most on stressed plants.
Spots on the grain carry it to the next crop.
sources: CropScan XR model class: Rice___Brown_spot, rice brown spot, Brown spot

diseases.name: Rice Tungro
diseases.pathogen: Rice tungro bacilliform virus with rice tungro spherical virus
diseases.description: A virus disease of rice in South and Southeast Asia: plants are stunted and their leaves turn yellow to orange.
diseases.causes: Green leafhoppers (Nephotettix virescens) carry the two viruses from infected rice, stubble regrowth and weeds.
symptoms: Young leaves yellow to orange-yellow, starting at the tip
Plants stunted, with few tillers and small, partly empty panicles
diseases.untreated: Early infection over a whole area can lose most of the crop.

steps.title: Remove infected plants
steps.instruction: Pull out yellowed, stunted plants and bury them.
steps.rationale: They are the virus source for leafhoppers.

steps.title: Watch the leafhoppers
steps.instruction: Check leafhopper numbers and act as advised locally.

steps.title: Plough in stubble after harvest
steps.rationale: Regrowth keeps the virus going between crops.

prevention.title: Plant at the same time as neighbours
prevention.detail: Leaves no young rice for leafhoppers between crops.

lifecycle: Leafhoppers pick up the viruses from infected rice.
They carry them to young plants.
Leaves turn yellow-orange; growth stops.
Stubble and weeds keep the viruses between crops.
sources: CropScan XR model class: Rice___Tungro, rice tungro, Tungro
